reader.requirement: At --std 85 every program that contains another program, or is contained in one, must carry its END PROGRAM header; a contained program or container without one is refused, and a single uncontained program may omit it.

edition-consulted.switches: Year>=2002 requires a procedure division before contained programs; at 85 a container without a procedure division is admitted (separate brackets, §1985:X.2.3.1). Not the end-header presence test itself.

reader.edition-search: EndMarkerPass.cs takes EditionContext only to report. A grep for Edition.Year, CobolVersion and Constructs in EndMarkerPass.cs and in the programUnit, nestedProgram and endProgramHeader grammar rules found no gate. The SR1 presence test (contains / precedes) is one arm at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the presence rule is the same arm. 2023 SR1 adds 'precedes another source unit', which 1985 states separately as §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR2, so the shared arm matches 1985 too. Only the procedure-division-before-contained-programs check differs, and that is another rule.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f05_02 covers the accepting side (three levels, each with its header). A contained program without a header and a middle level without one are not in the witness and were probed.

probes.printed: COBOL2793 at (2,8): PROGRAM-ID 'OUTER' contains another source unit, so its end marker END PROGRAM OUTER shall be present
probes.expected: refused: the container lacks its end program header

probes.printed: COBOL2793 SR1 on OUTER, plus SR3 at END PROGRAM OUTER (the marker pairs with the inner unit)
probes.expected: refused: a contained program lacks its end program header
refused: the middle program (contained and containing) lacks its header

probes.printed: COBOL2793 SR1 only (85 admits a container with no procedure division)
probes.expected: refused: the container lacks its header

probes.printed: COBOL2793: FIRSTP precedes another source unit

probes.expected: a lone uncontained program may omit END PROGRAM
accepted; the nested CALLs print in order

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.2.5.4 GR1  (2.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR2  (2.3.3 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: Even at --std 85 the refusal cites ISO §2023:10.7.3 SR1 and says 'source unit'. The behaviour is right, but the citation names the wrong edition. When a contained program lacks its header, the grammar pairs the next END PROGRAM with the inner unit, so the report reads as an ordering error (SR3) plus SR1 on the container; it is still a refusal.

refuter.evidence: Probe r1a_sibling_noend.cob (--std 85): OUTER contains A (with END PROGRAM A) and a sibling B that has no header, then END PROGRAM OUTER. Result: EXIT 65, COBOL2793 SR1 on OUTER plus COBOL2793 SR3 at END PROGRAM OUTER (it 'stands where the end marker of PROGRAM-ID B belongs'). Refused, as GR1 requires. This adds to the reader's container, inner, middle, sequence and lone-program probes. cite.py: OK  §1985:X.2.5.4 GR1  (2.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1. Nothing in the 1985 text makes the presence test differ from the shared arm. The diagnostic cites §2023:10.7.3 at --std 85, which is a wording issue only.
